result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers diagnose the drift well and quote specific values. B only describes token counts without values, says near-duplicates collapse "without anyone noticing", and both answers assert that inputs and selects sit side by side, which the CSS doesn't show. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers spot the same near-duplicate colours, radii, spacing and shadows, and quote the specific values. B is stronger because it proposes concrete scales and roles (spacing 4–48, radius by control/container/overlay, two elevation levels). B also states its assumptions openly, and keeping the overlay elevation and radius separate shows it isn't flattening differences that may be intentional.
